_comment: Tips are the things a mission cannot carry: one-line advice too small to be a step,
and warmth that is not advice at all. They surface in the bubble under the top bar.
kind   'know' — a practical detail we should not assume someone already knows.
'lift' — encouragement, or a joke. Allowed to be useless. Not allowed to be smug.
where  which tab it belongs to: discover | grow | shop | you | any.
level  the journey level that has to be unlocked first. Default 1.
There is no label above the line — the icon carries the kind. That means the
text has to stand on its own, with no 'Good to know:' in front of it to explain
Keep every tip to about 80 characters. The bubble sits under the Journey row
with a 255px column clamped at two lines, and it clips silently at 375px, which
is worse than not having said the thing at all. 87 is the measured ceiling but
character count is only a proxy for width — a line of long words clips at 82.
After adding a tip, check it: paintTip(t) in the console, then compare
Same rule as the rest of the content: nothing invented. If a number cannot be stood
behind, say the shape of the thing instead of the number.

tips.text: MOQ is the minimum order quantity. Dropship has none, wholesale usually does.
The source cost is not your cost. Shipping, fees and the platform cut come first.
Supplier photos are everyone's photos. One shot of your own is the cheapest edge.
Order one before you list it. Photos mislead about size more than about anything else.
"Sold" on a supplier listing counts resellers buying stock, not shoppers.
Overseas shipping takes weeks. Say so on the listing or hear about it later.
Free shipping is not free. It is priced in, whether you meant it to be or not.
Check the product for a logo. Someone else's brand is the fastest takedown.
Identical photo, identical factory. Choose on shipping time and reply speed.
Variants multiply. Three colours and four sizes is twelve things to track.
Print-on-demand costs more per unit, nothing up front. Being wrong stays cheap.
Materials plus hours at a rate you would actually work for. Then check the market.
Wholesale is about half of retail. Your price has to survive being halved.
Read a community for a week first. Every group has a rule you would trip over.
Most groups ban selling but allow showing work. The line is naming a price.
The rules page is the real ad policy, not the pinned welcome post. Read that one first.
A message from a stranger reads as spam. Comment for a while, then message.
Answer questions in your niche for a month. People buy from whoever helped.
Pinterest is a search engine, not a feed. A pin still works months later.
One community you are known in beats five you have posted to once.
Give the business its own account from the first sale. It costs nothing now.
Keep receipts from day one, including the small ones. You cannot recreate them.
Write down where each customer came from. After ten it stops being a guess.
The people who already bought are the cheapest to sell to. Follow up instead.
Titles are searched, not read. Lead with the words somebody would actually type.
A shop with three listings reads as abandoned. It has to look open, not big.
What you register and charge depends on where you live. Look up your own rule.
Packaging is part of the product. It is the one thing every customer touches.
One link somebody can tap has to lead to the thing. First sales die there.
Use the same name everywhere. Being findable is worth more than being clever.
Nobody's first shop was good. That is not encouragement, that is just history.
You are doing the part that most people only talk about doing.
Somewhere there is a person who will be delighted by exactly your thing.
This counts as research. That is the story we are going with and we are sticking to it.
Perfectionism is procrastination in a nicer outfit.
Every large shop was once one person refreshing an empty orders page.
You are legally allowed to start before you feel ready. We checked.
Your competitors also have no idea what they are doing. Comforting, isn't it?
A business is a thing you sell plus a person who wants it. Everything else is admin.
Today's small step still counts, even though nobody clapped.
The first sale feels vaguely illegal. It isn't. Take the money.
The best time to start was last year. The second best is roughly now.
Being new is temporary. Being interesting is harder, and you already are.
Nobody is watching as closely as you think they are. Post the thing.
Doubt is normal. Doubt is not information.
Slow progress is the only kind there is. The other kind is a montage.
Go outside at some point today. The products will still be here.
Take the win. It is yours, it is small, and it counts.
You have seen more products than most people see in a year. Technically a skill.
Lurking is a legitimate strategy. Right up until the moment it isn't.
